patterns.name: Subset Generation (Include / Exclude)
patterns.explanation: Generate all 2^N subsets by recursing with a 'choose to include or skip the current element' branch. The recursion tree has depth N and 2^N leaves.
patterns.when_to_use: Enumerate all subsets / power set, count subsets satisfying a property, partition problems where the brute-force is feasible (N ≤ 20).
patterns.intuition: Each element has two fates: in or out. The recursion captures this binary choice; the leaves enumerate all combinations.
common_pitfalls: Mutating a shared list and forgetting to undo on backtrack
Pushing a reference to the running list instead of a copy when collecting results
Recursing with the same index twice and exploding into N!
Using subset generation when N > 20 — switch to DP

patterns.name: Permutations (Swap-Based)
patterns.explanation: Generate all N! permutations by swapping the current position with each later position, recursing, then swapping back. Avoids the O(N) overhead of a 'used' array per call.
patterns.when_to_use: Permutations, permutations II (with duplicates), letter-tile possibilities, anywhere you need all orderings of a small N.
patterns.intuition: At index i, fix one of the remaining elements at position i (by swapping), recurse on i+1, then unswap. Each leaf of the recursion is one permutation.
common_pitfalls: Forgetting to swap back (corrupts the array for sibling branches)
Producing duplicates when input has duplicates — must skip equal swaps
Recursing with N! complexity when DP would suffice
Returning a reference to the working array instead of a snapshot

patterns.name: Backtracking with State Restore
patterns.explanation: Explore a decision tree where each branch makes a choice, recurses, and then *undoes* the choice before trying the next branch. The 'restore' step is what makes backtracking different from naive recursion.
patterns.when_to_use: N-Queens, Sudoku, word search, combination sum, generate parentheses, palindrome partitioning. Anywhere the search space is huge but pruning makes it tractable.
patterns.intuition: Backtracking = DFS over a decision tree + pruning + undo. Pruning cuts branches that can't lead to a valid answer; undo restores the shared state so the next branch sees a clean slate.
common_pitfalls: Forgetting to restore the state after the recursive call
Pruning too aggressively and missing valid solutions
Pruning too weakly and timing out
Using deep copies of state instead of mutate-then-restore (correct but slow)
patterns.complexity_signature: Exponential in branching factor; pruning is essential

patterns.name: Divide & Conquer
patterns.explanation: Split a problem into k smaller independent subproblems, solve each recursively, combine the results. Master theorem governs complexity: T(N) = a·T(N/b) + f(N).
patterns.when_to_use: Merge sort, quick sort, closest pair of points, Strassen-style matrix multiply, max subarray (D&C variant), majority element, count inversions.
patterns.intuition: If two halves of the problem can be solved independently and combined cheaply, total cost is the sum across the recursion tree — usually O(N log N) when combine is O(N).
common_pitfalls: Combine step that's secretly O(N²), wrecking the complexity
Subproblems that overlap (then it's DP, not D&C)
Not actually halving — recursing on size N−1 gives O(N²) instead of O(N log N)
Using D&C where simple iteration would be clearer
patterns.complexity_signature: Master theorem: typically O(N log N) when combine is O(N)

patterns.name: Decision Tree Recursion
patterns.explanation: Frame the problem as 'at each step, what decisions can I make, and what's the best outcome?' Recurse on each decision. Without memoization, exponential; with memoization, this becomes top-down DP.
patterns.when_to_use: Coin change, climbing stairs, house robber, target sum, partition equal subset sum — when the state is small enough that memoization will tame the exponential.
patterns.intuition: A clean recursive formulation has a return contract ('the best answer for this subproblem') and a small recursion body ('try each decision, take the best'). Memoizing the return is mechanical.
common_pitfalls: Mutating shared state instead of returning values (memoization breaks)
Memo key that doesn't capture all of the subproblem's state
Forgetting base cases or getting them off by one
Recursing with parameters whose ranges aren't bounded → memo explosion
patterns.complexity_signature: O(states × work per state) once memoized

patterns.name: Recursion on Linked Structures
patterns.explanation: Recurse along a data structure's natural shape: linked lists by `next`, trees by children, expressions by sub-expressions. The function's return value carries the answer for the subtree.
patterns.when_to_use: Tree height/diameter, list reversal (recursive), expression evaluation, JSON-like nested aggregation. Anything where the structure dictates the recursion shape.
patterns.intuition: Define the function's contract for *any* node, then assume the contract holds for its children and combine. This is mathematical induction in code.
common_pitfalls: Stack overflow on long lists or unbalanced trees
Recomputing the same subtree multiple times (use memoization or one-pass)
Failing to define the base case clearly
Mixing return-value recursion with mutation
